  WHY: The audit scope drops the old path because it no longer resolves to a file, so the stale finding keeps the PR held (awaiting_followups) until its follow-up closes some other way. The one-line fix is to add `--no-renames`. Severity disagreement: anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 rated it NIT; google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash rated it MAJOR. === FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh:905-915 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `git diff --name-only` enables rename detection (`-M`, 50% similarity) by default, so only the destination path of a rename is listed. The carry-forward filter (`(.file | …) as $p | any($touched[]; . == $p) | not`) treats a prior finding on the pre-rename path as untouched.
  WHY: scripts/security_audit.sh (`if (repo_root / relative).is_file()`) drops the missing source path from scope, so the finding is never re-verified, but the report still publishes `Carried forward (file untouched since <delta base>, follow-up open): <ids>`. The PR stays blocked until the follow-up is closed by hand or the cycles run out. Fix: `git diff --no-renames --name-only`.
- scripts/review_single_issue_security_pass.sh:595-603, 675; single_pass_delta_source 309-319 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The gate announces a delta re-audit and logs `delta_since=<since>` whenever the dispatch is accepted, without checking for the `Audited findings (base64 JSON):`/`Audited findings sha256:` payload. That payload is omitted when the encoded size is over 40,000 bytes (`reason=prior_findings_omitted`) and for results posted before this PR.
  WHY: The audit ends `outcome=full reason=prior_findings_unverifiable` and runs a full audit, so the public PR comment misstates the scope. Merges stay safe. Fix: skip `-f prior_findings` and the delta_note when the payload is absent, or reword the note.

  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
